archetype: Jeskai partner modal voltron: two command-zone payoffs that tax every card that moves (Shabraz: a counter and 1 life per draw; Brallin: a counter and 1 damage to each opponent per discard), closed by 21 commander damage from whichever the board favours, with the held wheel as the one-turn finisher that grows both and, under Consecrated Sphinx, kills the table outright (stack 009).

role_assignment.default_role: The developing engine, not the early beatdown. Both payoffs live in the command zone, which strategy:conversion.availability ranks as the location a payoff 'cannot be kept off the table, only taxed', so the opening turns go to mana, one commander and standing draw (Rhystic Study, Mystic Remora, Faerie Mastermind, Ghostly Pilferer, Smothering Tithe), pacing the pod slow until the pivot as strategy:multiplayer.pod-management prescribes for engine decks. Role is seat-relative (strategy:whos-the-beatdown): against a counterspell draw deck like the one in log 001 you do not own the long game and must be the beatdown on that seat; against creature boards your inevitability is the scaling commander (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock: 'an engine that scales').
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: Flip to the kill the turn all of these hold: a commander has resolved and survived a turn cycle; a wheel or a double-strike grant (Shu Yun, Embercleave, Blade Historian, Akroma's Will, Boros Charm) is in hand with the mana for it; protection is up (Flawless Maneuver or Deflecting Swat free with a commander out, or Grand Abolisher on the battlefield, which shuts the table out of exactly the turn you go); and the table's open mana has been counted (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window: 'assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal'). The go decision is hand-and-board arithmetic before the first spell (strategy:critical-mass.storm-math): a wheel pays Brallin the size of the hand discarded (engine.json wincon; stack 001: seven cards, 7 per seat), so count the hand, not the hoped-for draws.

engines.engine: Draw tax: +1/+1 counter and 1 life per card drawn; the flying commander-damage road. Multiplied by Teferi's Ageless Insight and Bard, King of Dale (every non-first-draw-step draw becomes two, by oracle text), Lae'zel (+1 counter per placement), Consecrated Sphinx (two draws per opponent draw).

engines.engine: Discard tax: +1/+1 counter and 1 damage to EACH opponent per discard; the each-opponent scope that strategy:conversion.yield prices at three times a targeted converter. Amplified by Torbran, Gratuitous Violence, Fiery Emancipation, Artist's Talent; doubled by Glint-Horn Buccaneer and Magmakin Artillerist.
engines.evidence: oracle text; verified stacks 001, 003 (a cycling cost discard triggers him), 004, 005, 007, 008, 009, 010

engines.engine: The one checker-passed table kill: a symmetrical wheel becomes an asymmetric draw flood (21 Sphinx triggers), Shabraz grows past lethal size and the cleanup discard fires Brallin until all three opponents are at 0. The symmetric refill problem of wheels is solved by Sphinx converting the table's draws into yours, the 'engine that out-draws three players' strategy:card-advantage names the format's defining advantage.

This is the line that answers the pilot's 'mana-starved' game 003 on the kill turn — an equip, a Shu Yun payment or a second wheel.

The same file lists [Brallin, Skyshark Rider, Curiosity] as a two-card loop, but Brallin has no discard outlet of his own, so that record needs a refutation stack before anyone believes it (agents-common §4: Spellbook lines can quietly assume a piece). Recorded for the pilot's watch list only; no add is recommended here.

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: You are the beatdown on that seat: the control deck owns the long game, and 'whoever loses the long game must be the beatdown' (strategy:whos-the-beatdown). Deploy in waves (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math): one commander first, the second held as the rebuild, which the partner pair gives you for free — the modal win means the second commander is a second threat, not a second piece (strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density, 'the median runs three cheap ones'). Flawless Maneuver answers a destroy wipe only; against exile and bounce the answer is a held counter (Negate, Stubborn Denial, Izzet Charm) or March of Swirling Mist. Do not open with a symmetrical wheel against a counterspell draw deck: it refills their hand and their inevitability; prefer loots, and wheel only under Sphinx or Grand Abolisher on the pivot turn (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window).
matchup_frames.vs_stax: You are the beatdown, racing the lock (strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial). Taxes hit this deck's velocity directly — Shu Yun, Jeskai Ascendancy and Artist's Talent all want many noncreature spells a turn — so recount the hand under the tax. Outs: Chaos Warp and Get Lost (any permanent / creature, enchantment, planeswalker), Prismari Command for an artifact; name the piece that beats you, not the scariest one. Lightning Greaves at equip 0 stays live under an equip tax that a 3-equip Embercleave does not.
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: Commander damage kills one seat at a time, and an attack opens you to the two seats you did not choose (strategy:conversion.combat-channel). Shabraz's 1 life per draw is a racing resource (strategy:combat-math.racing: spend the minimum that wins your race); Bard has reach and vigilance, Akroma's Will's second mode is lifelink and indestructible, and Incendiary Command's sweep mode clears small creatures. Brallin's each-opponent pings let you damage the aggro seat without turning sideways.
matchup_frames.vs_combo: Held answers rot against combo — 'the last profitable moment is now' (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy). Negate, Stubborn Denial and Izzet Charm counter the noncreature half of most combos; Grand Abolisher only protects your own turn, so it is a kill-turn piece, not a combo hoser. Your clock is not fast enough to ignore them (goldfish median kill turn 7 with no opposition, kill by turn 6 in 31.0%), so hold one counter rather than tap out for a value engine.

distribution_notes: From deck-facts (sha 0f00066d1090, matches goldfish_metrics): 100 copies, 36 lands (34 entries), 64 nonland; curve 1:8, 2:21, 3:18, 4:8, 5:5, 6:4. Mana is the soft spot. Red has 30 land sources against a deck-facts target of 36 and 39 red pips over 26 cards, with three triple-red payoffs: Torbran {1}{R}{R}{R}, Gratuitous Violence {2}{R}{R}{R}, Fiery Emancipation {3}{R}{R}{R}. Karsten's single-colour tables, quoted in strategy:deckbuilding.mana-base.color-sources, ask 33 / 30 / 28 sources for those costs, so 30 is short for Torbran on curve. That fits colour-on-curve R 88% against U 96% and W 91%, and land-drop hit rates of 79.4% on turn 4 and 70.8% on turn 5, beside the pilot's 'mana starved one round' in game 003. strategy:conversion.raising-the-ceiling's test applies: a deck that would do 'the same thing, twice' with two more mana has an input problem, not a payoff problem. Ramp is six cards (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Azorius and Izzet Signets, Talisman of Creativity, Smothering Tithe) plus Sorcerer Class's spells-only mana; it is drawn by turn 6 in 69.1%. There are eight wheels (engine.json wincon), and one is in 45.6% of opening sevens. That is near the 41% strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors gives for seven copies, so the job is holding a wheel, not finding one. The wheel-heavy hand from log 002 is the payoff-without-enabler keep that strategy:mulligans.engine-hands says to ship: the commanders cannot be drawn and are never the constraint, so the enablers are mana and protection. Protection: the protection:self role covers nine cards, plus Deflecting Swat's redirect and Grand Abolisher. That is above the 6-8 'Voltron' band in strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite, and protection is drawn by turn 6 in 84.2%. Removal is lighter than the 8-10 floor in the same section. There are three spot removal spells (Swords, Get Lost, Chaos Warp), three removal modes inside modal cards (Collective Defiance, Incendiary Command, Izzet Charm), Prismari Command for artifacts, and one sweep mode (Incendiary Command). Counters are three (Negate, Stubborn Denial, Izzet Charm). Interaction is castable by turn 6 in 39.0% of goldfish games. The commanders: Shabraz is cast by turn 6 in 87.7% (mean turn 4.928), Brallin in 95.8% (mean 4.015), and both are online by turn 6 in 87.5%. These are ceilings, because the goldfish has no removal. Goldfish kill: median turn 7, mean 6.991, by turn 6 in 31.0%. The goldfish does not model the modal voltron plan, the equipment or interaction (CONTEXT.md), so these figures are ceilings on how often the pieces line up, not a verdict.
overall_assessment: Sharknado is playing an engine game that ends in a voltron turn. In strategy:conversion.availability's terms the deck is unusually well located: both payoffs sit in the command zone, so the question is never whether a payoff shows up. It is whether one survives and whether the hand can be converted on the turn you choose. That makes it a commander-insurance deck first (strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance), with the twist that the partner pair turns the recast tax into a second, independent threat. strategy:deckbuilding.threat-density's 'Plan A and Plan B' fits better than usual because the two plans are layered rather than unconnected: every wheel and loot feeds both commanders at once. Brallin's scope is each-opponent, the yield strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry and strategy:conversion.yield favour against 120 combined life. Shabraz's is single-seat combat, which pays strategy:conversion.combat-channel's three taxes, so the flyer is the clean seat-killer and the pinger is the table-softener. The one proved table kill is Wheel of Fortune under Consecrated Sphinx (stack 009), which wins precisely because Sphinx makes a symmetrical wheel asymmetric. The pilot's own thesis, wheels as finishers fired with a commander out, is the strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection prescription in his words: time the tells for the turn they win, not the turn they impress. It also answers the political cost he named in log 002 (strategy:multiplayer.politics: a table you play again is a multi-game resource). Three things hold it back, all grounded above. Mana: red is short for the triple-red amplifiers, and game 003 was mana-starved. Proof: the stated win condition, 21 commander damage with a double-strike grant in the 99, has no passing stack (candidate lines 1, 2, 5 and 6). Removal: the count sits below the interaction-suite floor even after answers-v1. This frame is ★ coaching. It verifies no line, and nothing in it upgrades a candidate to fact.

It would cover 21 per seat against 40 life, kill order across three seats, evasion versus double strike as the scarcer piece, equipment versus intrinsic growth, and the shroud-blocks-your-own-equip sequencing trap with Lightning Greaves. Replacement-effect stacking for damage and draw doublers (Torbran, Gratuitous Violence, Fiery Emancipation, Artist's Talent; Bard and Teferi's Ageless Insight): the affected player orders damage replacements, so a build should price the smaller result. No section covers it. Carried; still missing.

Removal counts for a voltron or engine deck that leans on protection: whether a deck above the protection band can run below Walser's 8-10 removal floor. strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite gives both numbers but not the trade between them.
